When this DNA is disrupted, it leads to significant errors in pairing, ultimately affecting fertility by causing the body to eliminate improperly paired egg cells. This finding may also have implications for understanding reproductive barriers between closely related species due to variations in satellite DNA content.

 - Errors in chromosome pairing can lead to reduced fertility in fruit flies.

A framework called Hydra has been developed for characterizing workload inference in edge system-on-chip (SoC) architectures, taking into account factors such as backend structure, model quantization, and hardware telemetry. The study evaluates multiple generations of SoC and various instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) to provide insights into performance and efficiency metrics, addressing how deployment effects can impact latency and resource utilization. Hydra's findings and collected data are publicly available, promoting reproducibility in edge LLM inference characterization.

 - Hydra provides a multi-dimensional framework for LLM inference characterization across various edge SoC architectures.
 - The analysis conducted reveals nuances in performance and efficiency that are not evident when merely assessing aggregate latency.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25053
